title: Persona protocols and instrumentation notes for chat onboarding
content:
Purpose

This doc captures the pragmatic protocol we iterate on during model onboarding for chat: how personas are encoded/specified, the canonical system prompt patterns, explicit tool-calling contracts, and the instrumentation we require for regression detection and root-cause. Think of this as a cross-team checklist (Applied ML, Runtime, Console) rather than a formal spec.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to chat-style endpoints where we might attach a persona/system prompt, allow tool calls (search, database-read, exec), and apply safety scaffolds (pre/post filters).
- Target models: open/quantized variants we expect to host in Dedicated/Hosted.
- We assume the runtime can tag requests with request_id, model_version, persona_id, and emit structured events to our observability pipeline.

High-level goals
- Make persona behavior auditable and sufficiently instrumented to detect regressions quickly.
- Standardize tool-call protocol so downstream infra can route, retry, and measure cost/latency accurately.
- Surface safety scaffold activations and false-positive/negative trends in daily dashboards.

Definitions (quick)
- persona_id: short stable slug for the persona (e.g., concise-dev-v1).
- system_prompt: persistent prefix inserted by platform (not user-visible) used to express persona invariants.
- user_prompt: end-user content / message history.
- tool_call: structured output from model indicating an external action (name + args).

Persona encoding guidelines
- Keep persona_id stable across micro-updates; change only on semantic shift.
- System prompt should be < 300 tokens for bandwidth predictability; prefer bulletized invariants.
- Separate "voice/style" from "capability constraints". Example pattern below (SYSTEM template):

  [SYSTEM] Persona: concise-dev-v1
  Role: You are a concise developer assistant for engineers.
  Tone: concise, direct, use code blocks for code, and short examples.
  Constraints: Never fabricate access to customer data; when unsure, admit uncertainty and propose a deterministic check.
  Tool policy: Use tool-calls only for facts or external queries. If user asks about private data, escalate to safe-fail.

Persona example (literal):
"You are ConciseDev (persona_id: concise-dev-v1). Keep replies < 6 sentences unless user asks for a deep dive. When code is provided, return a runnable snippet in the requested language. If the answer depends on runtime state, include a clear \"I may be outdated\" line and offer a tool call for verification."

Tool-calling protocol (runtime contract)
- Model output must be explicit JSON-ish tool-call wrapper when invoking tools: e.g. TOOL_CALL(name:search, args:{query:"..."}, confidence:0.88). We prefer the runtime to detect structured tool intents via a deterministic parser.
- Required fields emitted with each tool invocation in the logs: tool_name, tool_args_hash, tool_call_id, start_ts, end_ts, tool_status (success|fail|timeout), tool_response_length.
- Retries: runtime should apply exponential backoff; model should include idempotency hints in tool args when necessary.
- Fallback semantics: if the model generates an unrecognized tool name, runtime should return a safe human-readable warning to the user and route the original model output to debug logs for postmortem.

Safety scaffolds and instrumentation
- Two-layer approach: pre-response filter (blocked content; early deny) and post-response classifier (safety_score, hallucination_risk).
- Emit per-request safety metadata: safety_triggered(true/false), safety_reason_codes(list), safety_score(0-1), safety_action(take: block|warn|tag).
- Compute and store: per-model daily counts for safety_trigger_rate, false_positive_rate (via sampling/evals), and false_negative_estimate (via user reports and retrospective evals).
- Regression triggers (automatic alerts):
  * absolute rise of safety_trigger_rate by >2 percentage points vs 7-day baseline and count > 50/day.
  * relative increase in false_positive_rate by 30% and >10 absolute FP/day.
  * hallucination metric (task-specific) degradation >5% relative.
- Instrumentation detail: emit events at these checkpoints: request_received, persona_applied, prompt_length, kv_cache_hit (bool), model_inference_start, model_inference_end, tool_call_initiated, tool_call_completed, prefilter_eval_result, postfilter_eval_result, response_sent. Include request_id and trace_id on all events.

Logging schema (recommended fields in each event)
- request_id, trace_id, timestamp, model_version, persona_id, user_id_hash, prompt_hash, input_length_tokens, response_length_tokens, avg_token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, tool_call_ids(list-of-ids), safety_score, safety_triggers(list), rollout_flag(canary|stable|disabled).
- Keep fields flat for quick indexing. Do not log PII. Use hashing for user identifiers.

Onboarding test harness (must run for every model + persona combo)
- Smoke tests (fast):
  * persona consistency: 50 seed prompts that verify tone/length constraints.
  * tool invocation format: 30 prompts that should result in structured tool calls with valid args.
  * safety baseline: 100 adversarial prompts (from curated corpus) to validate prefilter blocks ~>= expected FP/FN targets.
- Regression suite (nightly):
  * task-specific metrics: precision/recall for retrieval answers; code correctness heuristics; factuality checks against ground-truth corpora.
  * sampling evaluation: 200 sampled chats compared to golden answers using scoring harness in evals/.
- Canary metrics to watch during rollout: average latency, per-route error rate, safety_trigger_rate, tool_call_failure_rate, mean tokens per response, user-sentiment proxy (thumbs-down rate).

Example regression alert thresholds (suggested)
- Latency: p95 increases by >20% vs baseline for >30 minutes.
- Safety: safety_trigger_rate increase >200% relative AND >100 triggers/day.
- Tool reliability: tool_call_failure_rate >3% for 1 hour.

Prompt templating and variable injection rules
- Never inject raw user text into system_prompt. Compose user content into a user section only.
- For variable insertion into templates, escape JSON and use prompt_hash to tie logs back to template.
- Keep template parameters explicit (e.g., {{user_question}}) and documented in the persona manifest.

Observability dashboards to create (owner per dash)
- Persona health overview: per-persona p95 latency, safety triggers, FP sample rate, avg tokens, model_version mix. (owner: eng-applied-ml)
- Tool health: per-tool latency/throughput/failure rate + top failing arg patterns. (owner: infra-runtime)
- Regression inbox: rolling alerts for onboarding failures and canary deviations; links to sample chats for triage. (owner: product-hosted-api)

Sample onboarding checklist (practical)
- [ ] Add persona manifest to model registry (persona_id, system_prompt, voice_sample, allowed_tools).
- [ ] Wire persona_id into runtime canary config and ensure logs propagate.
- [ ] Run smoke tests (persona & tool format). Attach failing samples to PR.
- [ ] Run safety adversarial suite and record FP/FN baseline.
- [ ] Deploy canary (5% traffic) with enhanced logging for 48h.
- [ ] Evaluate canary metrics against thresholds. If any fail, rollback and annotate root cause.

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we version persona system_prompts across model variants in a way that keeps older conversations reproducible? (proposal: manifest-level semantic version + patch notes).
- Can the runtime expose a "persona-similarity" metric to detect drift when new model variants are onboarded? (needed for automated rollback heuristics).
- Determine default sampling rate for storing full_chat_text for post-hoc evals that balances privacy and debugging needs.
- Integrate test harness with Optimize to get automatic batching/quant suggestions for each persona workload.

References and related artifacts
- Onboarding checklist (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Persona+Onboarding+Checklist
- Jira epic for regression harness: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/AI-1207
- Example model manifest PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry/pull/456

Quick notes-to-self for next iteration
- Add a small library of persona-specific adversarial prompts (e.g., hallucination prompts for finance data, impersonation vectors).
- Pilot a lightweight "explainable tool call" mode where the model emits a short justification with each tool_call (helps debugging).
- Work with privacy to finalize hashing policy for user_id_hash and sampling rules.

End of notes.

(If you're triaging: start with the sample failures in the PR linked above, then run the persona consistency smoke set in tools/onboarding/quick_checks.)
